subject: relationships
topic: Making a friend takes more hours than you expect
angle: Friendship closeness is associated with the amount of time spent together, shared leisure activities, and specific types of everyday talk.
title: The Price of Closeness

hooks.text: Who are you spending your hours on?
You think closeness is instant. It is measured in hours.
You are trading your time for your self-esteem.
Two chairs and a long conversation.

reveal.headline: Singles invest more in friendships for self-esteem.
reveal.body: Greater friendship investment predicts higher friendship quality and self-esteem later on. This association is stronger for single people than for those in partnerships.

explain.headline: Closeness is a product of shared time.
explain.body: Hours spent together and engagement in leisure activities are associated with closer friendships. Two types of everyday talk also predict changes in closeness.

matters.headline: Time is the currency of connection.
matters.body: That may be why your sense of self-worth is tied to the hours you spend with others. Your social circle may be a reflection of your time budget.

example.headline: The coffee shop table.
example.body: You sit across from a friend for two hours. You do not talk about big plans. You talk about the weather and your day. This is the work of closeness.

verdict: The evidence shows that time spent together and engagement in activities are associated with closer friendships and higher self-esteem, particularly for single individuals.
caveat: The studies primarily show associations rather than proving that spending time together is the direct cause of friendship closeness.
caption:
Friendship closeness is tied to the time you spend together. 

Research shows that hours spent together, leisure activities, and everyday talk are associated with closer bonds and higher self-esteem, especially for single people. These studies show associations rather than proving direct causation.

How much time do you actually spend with your friends?
